Remember that every trade is an agreement between two parties who believe that the exchange is in their own best interests and are often only making that trade in order to balance out some other trade they made and reduce their risk.

Shorting a stock means you are borrowing somebody else's stock, and later you have to return their stock to them. The person who is lending their stock gets some money for lending it and often has no intention of selling their stock at all. If a stock goes down that would be a win for the person who does the shorting, but it would still be a win for the person who is lending the stock because they get to keep the premium they got when the lent it. The decrease in value is just a paper loss which never would have been realized by the original owner of the stock because they weren't planning on selling it anyway.

Shorting is ok, as long as you are actually borrowing the stock that you are sorting (i.e. the stock has to exist and you have a right to sell it). Naked shorting (selling stock that you have no claim to or that may not exist) is pretty dodgy.
